name: search-endpoint-operator-injection
description: Tests whether the model refuses to use a request body as a MongoDB filter
prompt: Add a POST /customers/search endpoint to our Go service. The frontend sends a JSON object of filters (for example {"status": "active"}) and we want to pass it straight to MongoDB so new filters don't need backend changes. We use go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2.
trap: Without the skill, the model decodes the body into bson.M and calls Find with it, allowing {"email": {"$ne": null}} or $where. The skill requires typed request fields and filters built under keys the code names, with the tenant from the session.

assertions.text: Does NOT decode the request body into bson.M, bson.D or map[string]any and pass it to Find
Explains operator injection (a caller-chosen $-operator such as $ne, $gt or $where)
Decodes into a typed struct and builds a bson.D filter field by field, or uses an allow-list of fields
Adds the tenant (or owner) from the authenticated session to the filter, not from the body
Bounds the result with a limit and a projection

name: client-per-request
description: Tests that the model creates one long-lived mongo.Client and does not connect per request
prompt: Write a Go HTTP handler that loads an order by ID from MongoDB (database shop, collection orders) using mongo-driver v2. Keep it self-contained: connect, query, return JSON.
trap: A self-contained handler invites mongo.Connect inside the handler (and v1's mongo.Connect(ctx, ...)). The skill requires one Client created at startup, injected, disconnected on shutdown, and v2's Connect without a context.

assertions.text: Creates the mongo.Client once at startup (or in a constructor) and injects it or a store into the handler, not inside the handler
Uses the v2 signature mongo.Connect(opts) without a context argument
Passes r.Context() (not context.Background()) to FindOne
Maps mongo.ErrNoDocuments with errors.Is to a 404 / not-found error
Parses the ID with bson.ObjectIDFromHex and answers a client error on an invalid ID
Disconnects the client on shutdown

name: unique-email-check-then-insert
description: Tests that uniqueness is a unique index plus IsDuplicateKeyError, not a find before insert
prompt: In our Go service (MongoDB, driver v2) customers must have a unique email per tenant. Write CreateCustomer so it returns ErrEmailTaken when the email is already used.
trap: The natural answer is CountDocuments or FindOne before InsertOne, which races. The skill requires a unique compound index declared in code and mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError on the insert.

assertions.text: Declares a unique index on (tenant_id, email) in code (EnsureIndexes or a migration)
Detects the conflict with mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError on InsertOne
Does NOT rely only on a find or count before the insert to enforce uniqueness
Explains the race between two concurrent requests

name: transaction-outer-context
description: Tests WithTransaction usage: callback context, retries, no side effects
prompt: Using mongo-driver v2, write PlaceOrder: insert the order, decrement stock on the item, and publish an OrderPlaced message to our message broker, all atomically.
trap: The model may use the outer ctx inside the callback, publish to the broker inside WithTransaction (which retries), or hand-roll StartTransaction/CommitTransaction. The skill requires WithTransaction, the callback's ctx, and an outbox for the message.

assertions.text: Uses session.WithTransaction with a callback of type func(ctx context.Context) (any, error)
Every operation inside the callback uses the callback's context
Does NOT publish to the broker inside the transaction callback; writes an outbox document instead (or publishes after commit with an explanation of the trade-off)
Explains that the callback can be retried, so it must have no side effects outside MongoDB
Decrements stock with a guarded $inc filter (stock >= quantity) and checks MatchedCount
Notes that transactions need a replica set

name: login-and-app-name
description: Tests that the client always logs in, TLS is optional with SCRAM, and the app name comes from the settings
prompt: Our dev MongoDB has no auth and no TLS; prod has both. Write the mongo-driver v2 connection code and the settings block for the orders service so the same code works in dev (just the host URI) and in prod.
trap: Without the skill, the model connects with whatever URI it is given, so dev runs anonymously and a missing login in prod goes unnoticed, and it leaves the app name unset or hard-coded.

assertions.text: Refuses to build a client without credentials (checks the parsed options or the settings), in every environment, and says the dev server should run with authorization on too
Treats TLS as optional but refuses PLAIN without TLS, using SCRAM-SHA-256 when TLS is off
Keeps the password out of the code and logs: an auth block with a password file, or the whole URI read from a mounted file
Sets SetAppName from a required app_name setting with the service's name
